newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle market light at $72 - feedlot.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle market light at $72 - feedlot.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Friday traded in light numbers at $72.00 per cwt, unchanged from active sales at midweek, feedlot sources said.
About 500 head traded in Kansas and about 500 sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Okahoma areas, they said.
Most of this week's showlist was sold despite having a large number of cattle on feed 85 to 100 days, instead of the usual 110 to 120, the feedlot sources said.
Firm packer demand was attributed to brisk beef sales as retailers fill orders for features after the Thanksgiving Day holiday on November 28, market sources said.
Beef movement at midday was strong amid mixed prices, which fueled expectations for steady to firm feedlot cattle prices early next week, the sources said.
Beef was quoted down $0.32 to up $0.72 per cwt, with heavyweight choice down $0.21 at $115.95, according to USDA. The heavyweight choice value was up $2.51 since last Friday.

There were 254 fabricated loads sold at midday, which brought the week to date figure to 1,206 fabricated loads, versus 1,046 all of last week. Beef production this week was pegged at 462.5 million pounds, down 5.5 percent from the previous week and down 3.3 percent from a year ago.
